A phrasal verb = verb + particle (*up, down, on, off, out, away, back…*); only the verb changes: *picked up, is giving up, has run out*.

**Separable** — a noun object goes in the middle or after:
*Turn **off** the light. = Turn the light **off**.*
**A pronoun — only in the middle:** *Turn **it** off.* (not ~~turn off it~~)
Common: *turn on / off, pick up, put on, take off, give back, fill in, throw away, wake up, try on*

**Not separable** — the object goes only after the particle: *look **after** the kids → look after **them***
Common: *look after, look for, get over, run into, come across*

**Three-part** — always together: *look forward to, run out of, get on with, put up with*

**No object:** *get up, grow up, break down, set off*
Фразові дієслова — основа живої розмовно: Phrasal verbs are the basis of lively spoken English: native speakers say *find out*, not *discover*, *put off*, not *postpone*. The particle changes the meaning of the verb, so we learn the whole pair. And the grammar is just one thing: where the object goes, especially a pronoun.
